phrases.note: ty (informal): friends, family, young people. Pan (to a man) / Pani (to a woman): formal. Use the 3rd person: "Czy Pan mówi po angielsku?" (Does the gentleman speak English?). Use Pan / Pani when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Polish often drops the subject, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. Pan / Pani are the formal "you".

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Masculine: add -y or -i (or -e). Feminine: -a → -y or -i. Neuter: -o → -a. Some are irregular, so learn the plural with the word.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: Many verbs end in -ać or -ić. Pracować (to work):

grammar.title: Iść: to go
text: To go by transport use jechać (jadę, jedziesz...). Iść is on foot.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Order is flexible, but the usual order is subject, verb, object. Adjectives come before the noun and agree in gender and number.
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put nie before the verb. Double negatives are normal: nic nie mam.

Put nie before the verb. Polish uses double negatives: nic nie mam. "There is not" = nie ma + genitive: nie ma czasu. The object of a negative verb often changes to the genitive (mam samochód → nie mam samochodu).
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Yes or no question: start with czy, or just raise your voice.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: ty / twój for friends. Pan / Pani for strangers, with the verb in the 3rd person (he / she form). Add "Pan" or "Pani" + name or title.
ex: how are you? (formal, to a woman)

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: verb stem + -ł + person ending (masculine) or -ła (feminine). Future: będę + infinitive.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal (ty): often the stem or the stem + -j: czytaj! (read), chodź! (come). Plural (wy): -jcie / -cie. Formal: use proszę + infinitive. Negative: nie + the same form (nie czytaj!).

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: móc (can), musieć (must), chcieć (want) + infinitive: mogę pływać, muszę iść, chcę jeść. Nie wolno = you must not; nie musisz = you do not have to.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: w = in; na = on / at; pod = under; obok = next to; blisko = near; o dziewiątej = at nine. After w and na the place takes the locative ending: w szkole, na stole.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -szy / -ejszy to the adjective (większy = bigger); the most = naj- + comparative (największy). "Than" = niż: wyższy niż ja. Irregular: dobry, lepszy, najlepszy.
